summary:
ASTRA-MED is an AI-driven astronaut health monitoring and space-environment intelligence platform designed to support crew health awareness during long-duration space missions. It integrates physiological monitoring, personalized health baselines, predictive analytics, and environmental intelligence into a unified mission control system.

The platform monitors vital indicators such as heart rate, SpO₂, respiratory rate, body temperature, sleep, and physical activity. Its AI engine detects unusual physiological patterns, forecasts potential trends, and generates explainable health alerts. An astronaut digital twin provides an evolving view of individual health profiles, while NASA space-science resources offer environmental context through space weather, radiation-related information, and available ISS research datasets.

ASTRA-MED also features an AI-powered medical information assistant, mission timeline, emergency simulation, and interactive analytics dashboard. By combining astronaut health information with space-environment data, ASTRA-MED demonstrates an integrated approach to improving crew health awareness and supporting medical decision-making in future space exploration.
details: ASTRA-MED is an AI-driven astronaut health monitoring and space-environment intelligence platform designed to support astronaut health awareness and medical decision-making during long-duration space missions. HOW IT WORKS: ASTRA-MED collects and analyzes physiological indicators, including heart rate, SpO₂, respiratory rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep patterns and physical activity. Its AI-powered analytics engine uses personalized baselines, machine learning-based anomaly detection and time-series forecasting to identify unusual physiological patterns and generate explainable alerts. The Astronaut Digital Twin maintains an evolving representation of individual astronaut health profiles. The Space Environment Intelligence module incorporates relevant NASA space-science resources, including space weather, solar activity, radiation-related information and available ISS environmental research datasets. A mission timeline combines physiological and environmental events to support exploratory correlation analysis. The platform also includes an AI-powered medical information assistant using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), an interactive emergency scenario simulator, mission control dashboard, predictive analytics and incident reporting. BENEFITS AND IMPACT: ASTRA-MED aims to improve crew health awareness, support early identification of unusual physiological trends, provide personalized health insights and help mission operators explore potential relationships between astronaut health and space-environment conditions. Its modular architecture offers potential applications in future long-duration missions, space medicine research and remote health monitoring. TECHNOLOGY: The software architecture uses modern web development technologies, including Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, machine learning frameworks, PostgreSQL and interactive data visualization libraries. AI-assisted development tools, including Claude and ChatGPT, supported architecture design, coding, debugging and documentation. No dedicated medical hardware is required for the current software prototype; simulated physiological telemetry is used where real astronaut measurements are unavailable. CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION: The central innovation is integrating personalized astronaut health monitoring, predictive AI, digital twins and space-environment intelligence into one mission-oriented platform rather than treating these systems independently. DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS: The project considers data reliability, scientific validity, privacy, explainability, uncertainty, interoperability and the distinction between real measurements, historical research data, estimates and simulated scenarios. ASTRA-MED is an experimental research prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system or a replacement for professional medical judgment.
